newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Raffles Medical sets sights on overseas expansion.
newsitem.headline: Raffles Medical sets sights on overseas expansion.

text.p: Overseas expansion will be a driving force for soon-to-be-listed Singapore healthcare company Raffles Medical Group (RMG), its chairman said on Monday.
"I think it's reasonable to expect that more and more contributions will come from regional operations in future," RMG chairman Loo Choon Yong told reporters on Monday.
"The healthcare business is related to population size and you've only got to look at surrounding populations to realise the opportunities," he added.
Populations of about 200 million in Indonesia, around 80 million in the Philippines and some 20 million in Malaysia all offered significant market potential, Loo said.
Expansion would be concentrated on Singapore where RMG wants its clinic network number to rise to 50 from 27 by 1998.
About 500,000 of the 563,000 patients treated by RMG in 1996 were in Singapore and two thirds of the company's revenues are now generated by the clinic network.
But regionalisation plans were already in place and funds would be targeted at operations in Hong Kong which Loo hoped would be a jumping off point for expansion into mainland China.
Primary healthcare, RMG's core activity in Singapore, might not be the guise in which it entered foreign territory.
"We may well go in as hospital developers rather than as healthcare providers," Loo said.
A memorandum of understanding, signed with Singapore property group Pidemco Land to develop a private hospital in the city-state, would provide a suitable development partner.
The project -- currently under consideration -- would need up to Singapore $100 million and tapping into the equity or corporate debt market would be the route followed, Loo said.
He was speaking at the launch of RMG's initial public offering of 38.04 million new shares which aims to raise about Singapore $13.5 million, mainly to finance expansion.
Shares are being offered at S$0.38 each with 28.53 million shares offered to the public and 9.51 million being placed privately.
